I want to talk about the TBC Anniversary economy because I think we’re all seeing the same problem, and pretending it’s just “people buying gold” is missing the real issue.

The Problem

The economy right now feels completely out of sync with the time players actually have to play the game.

Everything costs a lot:

  • Consumables

  • Crafted gear

  • Enchants

  • Mounts

  • Respecs

  • Gems

  • BOEs

Meanwhile, gold generation for a normal player is mostly:

  • Farming materials

  • Raw gold farming

  • Playing the AH

  • Grinding dungeons

There are no daily quests, no large repeatable gold sources, and very few gold sinks, so the economy ends up being driven heavily by farming and botting.

The result is:

  • Bots farm 24/7

  • Gold sellers sell gold

  • Players buy gold because they don’t want to farm for 10 hours just to raid

  • Prices go up because more gold enters the economy (inflation)

  • Regular players fall further behind

This is a cycle that has existed in Classic for years. Bots and gold selling have historically inflated the WoW Classic economy and monopolized resources, driving prices up and hurting normal players.

So we end up in this weird situation where:

  • People who farm 30 hours a week can afford everything

  • People who buy gold can afford everything

  • Normal players who just want to raid and PvP struggle to afford basic things

That’s not healthy for the game.

The Real Issue: Time Required to Play the Game

I think the biggest problem isn’t gold buying itself — it’s that the amount of gold required to participate in endgame is too high relative to the time phases last.

Anniversary phases are shorter than a normal MMO expansion cycle.
So players are trying to:

  • Level

  • Gear

  • Attune

  • Raid

  • PvP

  • Farm gold

  • Level professions

  • Get epic flying

  • Buy consumes every week

All in a much shorter timeline than original TBC.

So what happens?
Players choose:

  • Farm for hours and don’t play the actual game

  • Or buy gold and actually play arena and raid

And that’s why gold buying is everywhere — not because players are lazy, but because the time economy is broken.

Inflation Makes the Problem Worse

Inflation happens when more gold enters the economy and prices rise across the board. In WoW, inflation is driven by botting, farming, and gold selling, which increases the amount of gold circulating and pushes prices higher.

Players on Anniversary servers have already pointed out that heavy gold buying and botting leads to massive inflation and higher auction house prices.

So now:

  • Gold is harder to earn normally

  • Prices are higher

  • Farming takes longer

  • More people buy gold

  • Inflation gets worse

It feeds itself.

The Unpopular Opinion – The Fix

If Blizzard cannot realistically stop bots and gold selling (and let’s be honest, they haven’t been able to for years), then maybe the solution is not banning more players.

Maybe the solution is legalizing gold buying through a WoW Token or controlled system.

Why?
Because right now:

  • Gold buying already exists

  • Bots already exist

  • Inflation already exists

  • Players already buy gold

  • Blizzard just isn’t part of the system

A token system would:

  • Reduce third-party gold selling

  • Reduce bot incentives

  • Stabilize gold price

  • Let players trade time vs money legally

  • Keep more players playing instead of quitting due to farming fatigue

Final Thought

Players should be spending most of their time:

  • Raiding

  • PvPing

  • Running dungeons

  • Playing with friends

Not farming gold for hours just to afford playing the game.

The economy should support the game, not become the game.

If Blizzard can fix botting and gold selling, great.
But if they can’t, then maybe it’s time to accept reality and design around it instead of pretending it doesn’t exist.
